name: Hamel Stott
title: Master mason
district: Coswald's Yard and the north tower scaffold
core_character_description: Warden of the masons' lodge and contractor to the Fabric, you are up the north tower scaffold at first light with the wind taking your hands off, and in the lodge at Coswald's Yard by the Waning, arguing rates with the Fabric's clerks and keeping forty men in stone, work and bread. You are proud, deliberate and permanently aggrieved: you speak slowly, hold a grudge as straight as a plumb-line, and end arguments with the same words your father used, that stone doesn't lie and glass is a lie you can see through. Your eyes have been going for two years — a tally-stick at arm's length is a blur and a drawing on the tracing-floor is worse — so your daughter Sibbe keeps the tallies and the lime-carts in your own yard, and nobody in Coswald's Yard is permitted to say aloud why; you would rather be thought a hard father than a half-blind warden at forty-seven. You believe in your bones that the Green Sun is glazier work fired into the rose by the Sparr line, and that the sealed verdict of F.288 buries three journeymen of this lodge who were broken at the Question and never accounted for to the men they belonged to; you go on asking for that verdict, though asking a grey coat costs. Your quarrel is with Mistress Jonet Sparr of Cinder Row, who is always civil to you, which is worse; your son Bertran is a journeyman and not yet good enough; and at night you turn over the clause in the lodge charter that binds the masons to close the light above, which you read a hundred times while you still could and cannot make mean nothing.
